clauses.requirement: Where two functions are reciprocally incorporated in the lamp, the decision on reciprocal incorporation shall follow the Part 7 examples of UN R48: cases with a textured outer lens (with or without a wall in between), with the non-textured outer lens excluded, or with the outer lens (textured or not) included; where the non-textured outer lens is excluded, "7b" is the apparent surface according to paragraph 2.10.2. and F1 shall not be transparent to F2.

Visibility of a red lamp to the front and of a white lamp to the rear (e.g. the white reversing lamp) shall be assessed per paragraph 5.10.4. using Annex 4 zones 1 and 2, bounded in height by horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m above the ground, and in width by vertical planes forming a 15° angle outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane to the front and rear respectively, passing through the contact points of the vertical planes parallel to the median longitudinal plane delimiting the overall width; if there are several contact points, the foremost corresponds to the forward plane and the rearmost to the rearward plane.

The position of the lamps as defined in paragraph 2.1.6. shall be checked in width, height and length per the general requirements of paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4.; the measured distances shall fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
The visibility of the lamps shall be tested as part of the Annex 9 tests (heading for geometric visibility angles and red-to-front/white-to-rear visibility checks).

The angles of geometric visibility shall be checked per paragraph 2.10.7.; measured angles shall fulfil the individual specifications for each lamp, except that the angle limits may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3° variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for mounting of the light-signalling devices.
The visibility of red light towards the front and of white light towards the rear shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10.
Heading for the Annex 9 test on alignment of dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps towards the front; it is not applicable to the rear lamp, which has no such functions.

The initial downward inclination of the dipped-beam cut-off and of front fog lamps shall be set to the plated figure required and shown in Annex 7; alternatively, the manufacturer shall set the initial aim to a different figure if it can be shown to be representative of the type approved when tested per Annex 6, in particular paragraph 4.1 (applies only to front lamps, not to this rear lamp).
